- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent high or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment swings from bullish to bearish (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00), model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days post-sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward; add 1–3% to forecast if recent 3-day average is rising.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day EWMA) to reduce noise and avoid false peaks.
- If sentiment is uniformly bullish (≥0.67) and price is trending down, model may misread sentiment; reduce forecast by 2–4% if sentiment >0.67 and price >10% below 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment is negative (0.00) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract downward momentum.
